english.title: Breach confidentiality of prosecutions office re identity of a person - Commissioners for Revenue and Customs Act 2005
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) disclosed information held by the Revenue and Customs Prosecutions Office in connection with any of its functions which related to a person whose identity was specified in a disclosure or could be deduced from it
english.legislation: Contrary to section 40(3) and (7) of the Commissioners for Revenue and Customs Act 2005.
english.pointstoprove:

english.notes:
(i) Section 40(2) of the Commissioners for Revenue and Customs Act 2005 provides that the offence does not apply to a disclosure
(a) which is made for the purpose of a function of the Prosecutions Office and does not contravene any restrictions imposed by the Director
(b) made to His Majesty's Revenue and Customs in connection with a function of the Revenue and Customs (section 25 of that Act)
(c) made for the purposes of a criminal investigation or criminal proceedings whether or not within the United Kingdom
(d) which in the opinion of the Director is desirable for the purpose of safeguarding national security
(e) made in pursuance of an order of a court
(f) made with the consent of each person to whom the information relates
and the offence is subject to any other enactment.
(ii) Section 40(4) of the Act provides exempts from the offence the disclosure of information about internal administrative arrangements of the Revenue and Customs Prosecutions Office (whether relating to a member of the Office or to another person)
(iii) Section 40(5) of the Act that it is a defence for a person charged with an offence under this section of disclosing information to prove that he reasonably believed
(a) that the disclosure was lawful OR
(b) that the information had already and lawfully been made available to the public.
(iv) A prosecution for this offence may be instituted only by the Director of Revenue and Customs Prosecutions or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions, section 40(8).
(v) Section 10 of the Interpretation Act 1978 states that any reference to the Sovereign reigning at the time of the passing of the Act is to be construed, unless the contrary intention appears, as a reference to the Sovereign for the time being. As such, references to ‘Her Majesty’ and ‘the Queen’ have been replaced in the wording of the notes above to state ‘His Majesty’ or ‘the King’, although this may not be the strict wording of the legislation.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 55(7) of the Commissioners for Revenue and Customs Act 2005 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
